where: tool/addons.js:160 genCard (Standby generators card, Testing row)
tool_says: gen=[fac*4*0.706/1000,fac*4*14.6/1000] → "about 4 full-load hours a year: up to ${fmt(gen[0])} t CO₂ and ${fmt(gen[1])} kg NOₓ (uncontrolled-engine upper bound, AP-42)"

The register formula is "units × kW × test hours at load", and each set, spares included, is load-tested at its own rating. The card's own unit count (s.gN × s.g.mw) is ignored. The 10.5 h a year of no-load running is also left out. So the card understates by the ratio of installed generator capacity to facility load.
evidence: Hand recompute, 1 MW IT: fac = 1×1.55×1000 = 1,550 kW; ×4 h = 6,200 kWh → 4.38 t CO₂, 90.5 kg NOx (what the card shows). plant.js:29: Q = 1.55 → gen1 (1.0 MW), gNeed = ceil(1.55/1.0) = 2, gN (n+1) = 3. AP-42 factors confirmed: NOx 0.024, PM 0.0007, CO₂ 1.16 lb/hp-hr → 14.6, 0.43, 706 g/kWh.

tool_says: 1 MW set aside serves about 26–68 Level 2 stalls (7.4–19.2 kW, 0.5 diversity)  [code: st=[500/19.2,500/7.4]]
problem: The factor 0.5 is applied the wrong way round. The register's source term is a 'simultaneity 0.5' (Silber 2024). A simultaneity factor is the share of chargers drawing power at the same moment, so peak = n × P_charger × 0.5. That gives n = P ÷ (0.5 × P_charger). The tool uses n = P × 0.5 ÷ P_charger, which is 4 times too few stalls. The register formula 'P_reserved × SF ÷ P_charger' has the same inversion.

But the formula is inverted under both standard conventions. A simultaneity factor (coincident peak ÷ connected load, ≤ 1) gives n = P ÷ (SF × Pc). The register only quotes Silber's abstract ('0.5 in most cases'), so his exact definition should still be checked in the full text.

The tool uses the raw gas price per MWh of gas and sets it against heat-pump electricity per MWh, with no 0.85. Demand comes from CEUD, which counts delivered fuel, not useful heat (the cards.js:107 comment says so). So each MWh of gas is treated as needing a full MWh of heat-pump heat. The receiver's saving per MWh of heat is understated by 15%, and the 'net' value, break-even distances and payback are skewed. Vancouver net: tool $10.9–18.4/MWh; with ÷0.85 it is $16.8–24.3/MWh (+35–55%). Edmonton: tool −$7.6 to −$2.0; with ÷0.85 it is −$6.0 to −$0.45.
evidence: formula_register.json quantities.price_ceiling.formula: 'fuel price ÷ boiler efficiency (0.85)'. Recomputed: Van v=9.305×3.6=33.50, pe=67.9, so 33.50−67.9/3=10.87 and 33.50−67.9/4.5=18.41. With 33.50/0.85=39.41 these become 16.78 and 24.32. Edm pe=43.68+2.53+0.0809×43.68=49.74, v=9.01, so −7.57 and −2.04. With 9.01/0.85=10.60 they become −5.98 and −0.45.
suggested_fix: Apply the register's ÷0.85 (gas-heated receivers), or convert CEUD delivered energy to useful heat (×0.85) before costing heat-pump electricity. The formula change is confirmed from the register; J.B. to choose how.

Combined with the missing ÷0.85, the Edmonton best case turns positive: (1.045+2.025)×3.6/0.85 = $13.00/MWh against $11.05 of heat-pump electricity at COP 4.5, or +$1.95/MWh. problem: The simultaneity factor is applied the wrong way round. Silber et al. define it as the share of installed charger power drawn at once. So a fixed reservation supports N = P ÷ (SF × P_charger), not P × SF ÷ P_charger. The tool's formula halves the 1 MW and then assumes every charger runs at full power, which is the same as SF = 1 on 500 kW. The result is 4× too low (1/SF²). If the SF 0.5 premise is kept: 1,000 ÷ (0.5 × 19.2) = 104 and 1,000 ÷ (0.5 × 7.4) = 270 stalls, against the 26–68 shown. The m² figures that follow (573–1,486 m²) and the opps.js:54 land check (need = st[1]×22) are scaled down by the same factor.

suggested_fix: Unverified, needs J.B.'s decision. With the definition as read, the formula would be P_reserved ÷ (SF × P_charger), giving about 104–270 Level 2 stalls per MW at SF 0.5. Whether SF 0.5 should apply to Level 2 at all is a separate question (see the next finding).

v1.reasoning: Confirmed on internal logic, without reading Silber. A simultaneity or diversity factor below 1 means not every charger draws full power at once. So a fixed reservation must support at least P ÷ P_charger stalls: 52–135 per MW at SF = 1. The tool shows 26–68, fewer than with no diversity at all. So 0.5 acts as a derating, not as simultaneity. Under the standard definition (coincident peak ÷ installed power), N = P ÷ (SF × P_charger): 104–270 stalls, 4× the figure shown. The m² figures (573–1,486) and the need = st[1]×22 check at opps.js:54 scale down by the same factor. Silber's exact wording of the definition is not held locally (sources/06:16 quotes only '0.5 in most cases'). The 104–270 correction is therefore left to J.B.

where: formula_register.json quantities[borefield].coef (same in tool/opps.json quantities.borefield)
tool_says: q = 12 W/m ground-only to 19 W/m with a dry cooler (derived from Zurmuhl et al. 2018, a 14.5 kW data centre, Ithaca, k 3.27 W/m·K)
problem: The 760 m field behind the 19 W/m figure is Zurmuhl's economic optimum for the ground-only GHP system, not a dry-cooler (hybrid) field. The paper only reruns the hybrid at that 760 m. So 12 W/m (1,248 m base field) vs 19 W/m (760 m optimised field) is a base-vs-optimised difference, not ground-only vs hybrid. Also, 14.5 kW is the equipment cooling load, not the heat sent to the ground: the ground also takes the heat pump's compressor work, and in the hybrid case the dry cooler takes part of the heat. Yet the register formula divides 'heat to ground (W)' by a q that was derived from the cooling load.
evidence: Zurmuhl 2018, https://pangea.stanford.edu/ERE/pdf/IGAstandard/SGW/2018/Zurmuhl.pdf, p.7 s.4.2.1: 'The economically optimal value is approximately 760 m' (GHP, Fig. 4); p.8 s.4.2.2: hybrid run 'for the previously optimized BHE length of 760 m'; p.2: '14.5 kWth' equipment cooling load. Recomputed: 14,500/1,248 = 11.6 W/m; 14,500/760 = 19.1 W/m.
suggested_fix: Relabel as '12 W/m (base 1,248 m field) to 19 W/m (economically optimised 760 m field, ground-only GHP; the hybrid was also run at 760 m)', and say q is cooling load per metre, not ground heat rejection per metre. Correct q for ground rejection: unverified — needs J.B.

v1.reasoning: Cannot be settled locally: no copy of Zurmuhl 2018 is held. The project's own note (sources/15c l.18) says '1,248 m base field → 760 m optimized field with dry cooler', the reading the claim disputes. Only the paper's pp. 7–8 can decide whether 760 m is the GHP optimum or the hybrid field. Arithmetic checks: 14,500/1,248 = 11.6 W/m; 14,500/760 = 19.1 W/m. One related point is locally confirmable: 15c l.188 defines heat to ground as P_IT × (1 + 1/COP), yet q was derived from the 14.5 kWth load. If that load is the equipment cooling load, the units are mixed. Borefield length is not computed anywhere in the tool JS (register and opps.json text only), so no displayed figure depends on it.
v1.evidence: sources/15c l.18, l.188–189; grep 'bore' in tool/*.js shows no L = Q/q computation. Page to check: https://pangea.stanford.edu/ERE/pdf/IGAstandard/SGW/2018/Zurmuhl.pdf pp. 2, 7 (s. 4.2.1, Fig. 4), 8 (s. 4.2.2).
